nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space and $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$. A point $x \in E$ is a critical point of $f$ when the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ vanishes, $f'(x) = 0$. Here $f'(x)$ is taken to be $0$ when $f$ is not differentiable at $x$, so such points are critical as well.
nodes.title: Critical point

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space, $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$, $a, b \in E$ and $\varepsilon, r \in \mathbb{R}$. The points $a$ and $b$ are separated by a mountain range of $f$ at height $\varepsilon$ and radius $r$ when $f(a) = 0$, $\varepsilon > 0$, $r > 0$, $f(y) \ge \varepsilon$ for every $y \in E$ with $\|y - a\| = r$, $\|b - a\| > r$ and $f(b) \le 0$.
nodes.title: Mountain range

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space. A function $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies the Palais–Smale condition when every sequence $(u_k)$ in $E$ such that $(f(u_k))$ is bounded and the Fréchet derivatives $f'(u_k)$ tend to $0$ in operator norm has a subsequence converging in $E$. Here $f'(x)$ is taken to be $0$ at points where $f$ is not differentiable.
